title: The AI Employee Map
content: Stop treating Claude Code as a chat box. Treat it as a new hire and give it what any person joining your company gets on day one. The episode builds this live around one example business and ends with a seven-day setup plan.
explanation: The shift is from prompting to onboarding: most of the quality comes from the environment you set up, not the words of a single request.

title: 1 · A workspace
content: A dedicated repo or folder where the agent's files, code and outputs live, separate from everything else.
explanation: Without a home, every session starts from zero and outputs scatter across chats.

title: 2 · Memory
content: Persistent notes the agent reads at the start of each session: decisions, preferences, facts about the project.
explanation: Memory is what turns a string of one-off sessions into accumulated experience.

title: 3 · A brief
hook: Who we are and how we work
content: A standing instruction file (such as CLAUDE.md) that describes the business, the stack, the conventions and the rules.
explanation: The brief is the onboarding pack: write it once, and every session starts aligned.

title: 4 · A clear ticket
content: Each piece of work gets a specific, scoped request with a definition of done, like a ticket for a human engineer.
explanation: Vague asks produce vague work. A ticket makes success checkable.

title: 5 · Eyes
hook: A way to see the work
content: Give the agent ways to look at what it built: screenshots, a browser, logs, test output.
explanation: An agent that can see its own result can catch and fix its own mistakes.

title: 6 · Review
content: Changes go through review, either a human reading a pull request or a second agent checking the diff.
explanation: Review is the quality gate that lets you trust more autonomy over time.

title: 7 · A schedule
hook: Work that runs without being asked
content: Recurring jobs on a timer: daily reports, checks, summaries, follow-ups.
explanation: A schedule is what makes it an employee rather than a tool you have to pick up.

title: 8 · Permissions
hook: What it may and may not touch
content: Explicit rules for which tools, files and actions the agent can use without asking, and which need approval.
explanation: Clear permissions let you say yes to more, safely, instead of approving every step.

title: One operating loop
hook: Product · feedback · docs · demos · review · recurring work
content: The eight pieces connect into one loop: the agent builds the product, reads customer feedback, keeps docs current, records demos, gets reviewed and runs the recurring work.
explanation: The example in the episode is a missed-lead responder for med spas, an idea taken from ideabrowser.com.

title: The seven-day plan
content: The episode closes with a seven-day plan to set up the whole map at your own pace, starting with the workspace and ending with schedule and permissions.
explanation: Quick self-check: which of the eight does your setup already have, and which one would most improve the work this week?
